Lord Vishnu (Maha Vishnu, in adjacent sanctum)

history.dynasty: Tradition associates it with the Guruvayur founding legend; under Malabar Devaswom Board since 2008
history.period: Tradition claims centuries of antiquity; one of the five prominent Shiva temples around Guruvayur and counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala
history.summary: Mammiyoor Mahadeva Temple is the Shiva counterpart of Guruvayur: legend says Shiva was meditating on the banks of the Rudra Theertham where Guru (Brihaspati) and Vayu brought the Krishna idol from Dwaraka; Shiva advised them to install Krishna there and moved across the theertham to the present site. Hence 'Mahimaiyur' (place of Shiva's glory), corrupted to Mammiyoor, and the belief that a Guruvayur pilgrimage is complete only after worshipping here. Shiva is worshipped in Rowdra Bhava facing east as Uma Maheshwara - a family form with Goddess Parvati on his lap and Ganesha, Subrahmanya and Ayyappa beside; a Vishnu idol stands in the adjacent sanctum (said to have been installed to pacify Shiva's anger). During Shivaratri, both Shiva and Vishnu are taken on elephant procession for Sree Bhootha Bali, followed by Krishnanattam by the Guruvayur Devaswom troupe. Sub-shrines: Ganapathi, Muruga, Dharma Sastha, Bhagavati, Naga deities and Brahma Rakshassu.

name: Mammiyoor Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Guruvayur is a temple town in Thrissur district, about 28 km northwest of Thrissur city. It is one of South India's busiest pilgrimage centres, its identity and economy revolving entirely around the Sri Krishna temple - hotels, prasadam shops, marriage halls and Devaswom services. Mammiyoor lies about 2 km from the Krishna temple, at the edge of town towards Chavakkad. The nearby Punnathurkotta fort houses the temple's elephant sanctuary.
